title: The Hand of Judgment and the Right Hand of Salvation
english: He asked to have obtained the length of days, so that he might have them immortally and without end. The length of days is received also by the one who has enlightened himself with the light of knowledge, as if he had a doctrine of truth enlightened within him; for each description of thought is a certain day.

The salvation of God acquires great glory for the king raised from the dead and for everyone rising together with him (Ps 20:6-8a). You will lay glory and majesty upon him, this glory which is according to the resurrection. And 'you will lay upon' signifies that even before this glory he had another, according to 'I glorified and again I will glorify.' And majesty is that which is becoming in great things. The becoming in great things has not happened concerning the Savior alone. For what is greater than to raise the dead and to walk upon the sea and his enormous miracles among those nearby? But even from his rising from the dead, the becoming in great things has exceeded for him; for he was taken up into the heavens and sat at the right hand of the Father, 'For you will give him blessing unto the age of ages.' All these things have exceeded for him, that blessing is given to him for the age of ages from the Father, by which he blesses those approaching him; then especially the curse having been turned for our sake, he redeemed us from the curse of the law regarding becoming mortal, through the blessing of Abraham (Gen 12:3). 'Rejoice him in joy before your face' (Ps 16:11). Oh, the same grace and peace are given from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ, the seed from God, such that the same joy from God and from his face comes to be; for the face is the exact imprint of his hypostasis. And these things shall happen concerning the king, hoping in God the Lord, finding himself being of those who hope. For having approached the expected things through experience, he rejoices before the face of God. And otherwise: since your image is a face, and this is the God the Word, the king becoming with this face makes his temple profitable and, becoming conformed to him, rejoices in joy.

Having received oil from the Most High to be anointed with oil of exultation, he possesses an impassable priesthood from the anointing, according to the order of Melchizedek, a priest unto the age (Ps 20:8b-9). For that he shall not be shaken shows that he will not soon see the worthiness from which he is shaken.

Changing into something else. His hand is not found for a few, but for all the enemies of God, bringing punishments upon them and warring against those set against the divine law, according to 'The Lord fights with a hidden hand against Amalek' (1 Sam 15:30). And perhaps he means by enemies those bringing in thoughtlessness and embracing ungodliness. For if these do not set God before them, the hand would be found distressing them and bringing rebuke upon them, so that then they might know what God stands over of those who sin. He says 'hating God' here regarding those committing sin. For if in keeping the commandments the love of the perfect God is completed, according to 'If anyone loves me, he will keep my word' (John 14:23), he who does not keep the word and the commandments of God hates God. And he who hates thus is said to be perishing. Since there is no expectation of the Savior coming, the right hand of God, to seek and save the lost, it is fittingly said: 'May your right hand bring all who hate you to prosperity' (Ps 20:10).

But by what does the right hand differ according to the writings? One should consider the hand set upon punishments, as 'Your hand has utterly destroyed them' (Ps 6:10), and 'Now having sent the hand, I will strike you' (Ps 77:10) (and indeed 'The hand of the Lord has laid hold of me' [Job 10:1]); but the right hand is upon salvation and other good things; for 'His right hand saved him', and 'He made the right hand of the Lord a power', and 'The right hand of the Lord saved me' (Ps 18:35), and such things. It is fitting, then, that even here he says the hand is found punishing the enemies, but the right hand is found for those who hate [Him], so that they might be found no longer in destruction.

Regarding Ps 20:10a, I think it is meant that they shall be cast upon the enemies; not that anyone is handed over for punishment to be cast as a furnace of fire always and continually, but as at the time of the shining of the divine face. And there also, 'the time' signifies not a duration of time but the kind of state of those capable of receiving the face of God. And I think also that the mention of the furnace was not in vain; for just as a furnace does not burn in vain or by chance, but for some useful purpose in baking bread or something similar, so also God sets punishments at the time to encounter such [people] as may be able to behold His face. title: The Face of God and the Morning Perception
english: Those being disturbed by wickedness and false glory, being agitated by the allurements of pleasure, God shall shake in His wrath, and those being disturbed by the expectation of punishment.

But these are not consumed by a fire that is entirely physical, but by that which follows the disease of the soul; rather, when the soul repents for the evils it has done, a penalty of fire pierces it, or when dissatisfaction arises in it, a fire analogous to the diseases of the body is generated.

For just as bodily foods, when consumed beyond what is necessary, having a disease-causing quality, raise fevers in those who have eaten them, so too, from these foods, a fitting fire will follow the wickedness and the worthless doctrines; it consumes them not by destroying their soul's essence (for it is indestructible) but their quality, according to which wood becomes hay, stubble, or weeds, so that when the things that joined them are consumed, the pure essence that was bound remains visible.

And here it is shown not that their essence is perishing, but that they bore fruit badly: 'for your works are weary and worthless' (Ps 20:11). Just as plants bearing perfect fruit project seed from that fulfilled fruit to become plants similar to themselves, so those having borne the seed of teachings in wickedness and impiety are cast down to make others like them, worthless and impious. God destroys this seed from among the sons of men.

'They turned evil toward him' (Ps 20:12) [referring to] the false doctrines concerning Him, attributing the cause of wickedness to Him; and the traitors and enemies of Him, having been proven, turned evil toward the Savior. It should be noted that evil is accomplished by turning aside, and not by straightness, as the good are [seeds].

For all the worthless, having turned aside, act against the incapable; for they deliberate treacherously against the one who will not suffer harm. Perhaps also every evil man, through whom one sins, deliberates a plan that is unable to stand, because wickedness is unstable and not abiding. 'For you will set them low; with the remnant you will prepare their face' (Ps 20:13). God does not turn away; He sets these low, making them capable of being a face. The silence of God allows one with a pure heart to contemplate His works and those following Him, so that observing His creation they may grasp His mind, and having cast off weakness to have a pure face, they approach God and give Him the face of God. Therefore he says: 'And in your remnants you prepare their face' (Ps 20:14a), for the remnants of God are those things above His sensible creations.

Since descending with our weakness, you took up something weak, O He who is stronger than men, having been crucified out of weakness, 'Exalt yourself in your power' (Ps 20:14b). It is terrible to take up through contemplation, but to sing is to act according to virtue. Contemplating the intelligible of the powers and acting according to them, we see and sing of your powers, you who ruled as a triumphal king against the devil and the opposing powers. It is also possible to declare the graciousness: we cry out to you, having ruled against death.

Morning perception is made straight by the rising of the sun of righteousness and the making of the beginning of the day; for the rising of the true light has laid an end to the night of ignorance and error and has shone a spiritual illumination. And that which begins toward the end of perfect illumination will arrive, through which all other spiritual things were spiritually completed at the end, not because of all other things, but it itself is nothing, which they also call the last, because no one desires anything above this, this being the ultimate good.

The prophecy of the present psalm points toward the end of the morning perception of David, that is, of him who was born of his seed according to the flesh. And this must be kept: he who guards the face, saying from beginning to end, no single change is found regarding the saying 'face'. And since the New Testament has taken words from the psalm as if spoken by Christ, it is necessary to interpret all of it from the face of Christ. title: The Nature of Salvation and the Divine Origin of Christ
english: For to say, 'My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?'—that God, my God, is what he does in many places in the Scripture (Ps 21:2). He does not wish to say this specifically: that the general and true God, being my God, is encountering me while I am being fought against and experiencing many afflictions; for why have you forsaken me? The voice is inquiring about the cause of the abandonment. Since he possessed a great purity with himself (for sin was not necessary), he did not believe he was being forsaken because of sin, but because of something else that is beneficial to the whole. He does not wish this to become manifest through himself suffering, but through those seeing him; for having known what was forsaken for their sake, they will praise him as Savior.

Therefore, let us speak the words of the transgressions, not the pronunciations concerning the transgressions. For just as we say a word of heaven by which it has become, and a word of the sun by which it has risen, so also we shall say the words of transgressions, and not that the transgressions themselves drew the Savior into his own body. But his body brought these words of transgressions before the passion, and having risen from the dead—he who is also said to have saved—he held the words of the aforementioned sins far from his salvation, having stripped off the ruling principles and powers that work the transgressions, and he triumphed over them in himself, speaking boldly upon the cross.

It is allegorical that the cry 'O how I suffer something' to you, my God, is not only regarding those surrounding him in affliction and darkness at night (Ps 21:3), but also regarding those who are bright and shining, to whom I will again cry 'O how something harmful might come from the snare.' The Savior, confessing these things concerning us, says: 'O how will you hear when I cry to you?' For it is to be read with an undertone: 'And at night I will cry out,' not being considered by me as madness; the ones surrounding him are the dark ones, those darkened by many circumstances, just as he himself says 'Why must I cry out to God?'—is he ignorant? For I know what kind of night-state is around me.
The fathers from whom I am according to the flesh (they are not the patriarchs) have hoped in you, desiring my illumination (Ps 21:5). But having hoped, they did not fail; they were rescued.

For they were delivered and rescued from death and the devil by me. For they themselves, having cried out to you, abstained from the salvation which is through me and from me. For they did not become despondent toward you, hoping; for they abstained from the things of hope and expectation.

Those saying these things are law-learners, being promise-givers, falsely glorifying regarding providence. For the same things would be said by one being struck by Isaiah, and others have suffered for the sake of piety. For we do not say that to be rescued and saved from those standing around as oppressors means to become something outside of them, but to bravely and through toil endure them, so that the mind might not be harmed by the right intention being cast out by the pains. We say, indeed, that the witnesses of the truth, having suffered ten thousand things and having died by tortures, were rescued and were saved from the tribulations; for those having come to be outside of the tribulations through denial were not only not rescued and saved from the temptations, but were also exhausted by them.

For perhaps he who is conceived of seed, having been brought to completion in the womb, having been filled with the time of birth, is thrust forth from that womb to the outside. But the Father alone thrusts the Savior out from the womb of the Virgin, not having been cast into her from the outside by seed, but having been thrust out from her, from the divine offspring. To other men, hoping and expecting the things to come happens after the fulfillment of the word has come to pass with ages. But the child from Mary alone hopes for perfection; for God holds the hope; for he was never born in wickedness, unlike all men who grasp at the good through ignorance and malice. And Isaiah says this: Before he knows good or evil, he disobeys in wickedness to choose the good. Before the becoming-man, Jesus alone possessed intimacy toward the Father; for his Father was God, and he himself was the Son of God. But after becoming flesh, he came forth from the womb having a relationship like the relationship to God.
